criteria.text: `GET /api/compare` without `bridges` returns byte-identical JSON to the pre-existing shape (no `bridge` key anywhere): the existing fixture assertion in `test/graph.test.ts`'s `describe('compareFor (issue #93)', …)` (`:1991` onward) passes unmodified.

`GET /api/compare?bridges=1` adds a `bridge: number` (never `undefined`, never missing) to every entry in `terms`, for a fixture recorte with at least one edge surviving `having count(*) >= 2` shared across both tracked people's scopes.
In that recorte, the highest-betweenness term has `bridge === 1`; every other scored term has `0 <= bridge <= 1`.
A term in `terms` with no co-occurrence edge at all has `bridge === 0`, never `null` and never absent.

`src/communities.ts` exports `betweenness`, keyed by the same `kind:term` id shape `linksQuery` produces, unit-tested against a hand-built path graph where the middle node's centrality exceeds the ends'.

`RulerItem`'s `bridge?: number` addition does not change any existing `test/layout.test.ts` assertion: a `rulerLayout` call with items carrying no `bridge` produces identical `words`/`overflow`/`x`/`half`/`height`/`width` output to before this change.

`rulerTerms` attaches `bridge` onto its emitted item only when the source `CompareTerm` carries it, and painting a term with `bridge >= 0.5` produces markup containing `class="ruler-bridge"`; a term below the threshold does not.

`test/invariants.test.ts`'s import-direction check still passes with `betweenness` added to `communities.ts` — `src/graph.ts` may import it, `communities.ts` imports nothing from `graph.ts` or `server.ts`.

`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass with `graphology-metrics` added to `package.json`, pinned exact; `test/bundle-freshness.test.ts`'s existing `/graphology/` regex (`:59-61`) still matches and still asserts the front-end bundle excludes it — no second assertion needed, verified rather than added.

`docs/api.md` states, and `test/docs.ts`'s `docsText` confirms, that `/compare` accepts a `bridges` parameter and that it is always computed live, never cached beyond the route's existing cache class — checked against page content as a whole, never a specific heading or file split.
`GET /api/people/:id/lenses` without `bridges` returns byte-identical JSON to today: the existing `lensesFor` assertions in `test/graph.test.ts` pass unmodified.

`GET /api/people/:id/lenses?bridges=1` adds `bridge: number` to every `terms` entry, the top term at `1`, every other in `[0, 1]`, an isolated term at `0`, on a fixture recorte where two lenses (for instance two `domain:` lenses) of one person share at least one surviving edge.
With `a === b`, `bridges=1` returns the same `bridge` values as the corresponding single-lens graph would: equal lenses produce finite scores, never `NaN`.

`lensesParams` includes `bridges=1`, and `paintLensRuler` painting a term with `bridge >= 0.5` produces markup containing `class="ruler-bridge"`; `paintLensDetail` for such a term contains "ponte", and for a term below the threshold does not.
The per-side edge statement is one builder used by both routes: `statements` exposes the compare and lenses edge texts, and both are pinned in `test/graph.test.ts`.
